The story is told entirely from the limited third-person perspective of a single, sympathetic protagonist, Barbara Lindner. It does not provide diverse perspectives, nor does it delve into the mindset, beliefs, or motivations of the only character who commits a repugnant act (the young shooter). In fact, the shooter's motives and final words remain completely unknown to Barbara and the rest of the congregation, which the story explicitly notes is "the thing people could least forgive."
